newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST-Bufete Q1 seen returning to profit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Bufete Q1 seen returning to profit.

text.p: First quarter results from Mexican construction company Bufete Industrial are expected to show the company has used an economic turnaround to build a return to profitability.
A survey of four industry analysts saw average earnings per share during the quarter of 0.086 pesos, compared with a net loss of 0.58 pesos in the same period of the year before.
Revenues are seen at an average of 1.14 billion pesos and operating profits at 57.5 million pesos, up 7.2 and 47.7 percent, respectively, compared with 1996's first quarter.
"Bufete is doing better (than other Mexican builders), the outlook of their business is much clearer than before," said Hector Castillo, an ING Barings analyst in New York.
"Its projects are being carried out well, which gives stability to revenues and margins," Gerardo Saenz, an analyst at Serfin brokerage in Mexico City, wrote in a recent report.
He added that an expected improvement in margins was due to cost controls and a better mix of projects in progress.
Despite the generally good picture, some analysts said Bufete could still report a quarterly net loss due to start-up costs for some projects that have not begun to earn revenues.
And some analysts said they did not see the builder reporting higher receipts from the Federal Electricity Commission (CFE), one of its main clients.
"The main issue is still the account receiveable with the CFE and there is no indication that they collected it during the first quarter" said Chris Hussey, an analyst at Goldman Sachs in New York.
Bufete's backlog is seen falling slightly during the quarter. Saenz estimated the company would report a backlog of 2.979 billion pesos, down 10 percent compared to the end of 1996.
